content:
Just found this app.

Then somehow spent HOURS making screenshots for it.

Make that make sense :)

That was the specific problem I had:

I wanted my App Store visuals to actually explain the product and look polished, but I didn’t want to design every layout, device mockup and graphic from scratch.

Because here’s something app builders underestimate:

Your App Store screenshots are basically your landing page.

People are scanning them to decide:

→ What does this app do?
→ Is it useful for me?
→ Does it look trustworthy?
→ Is it worth downloading?

So I tried AppLaunchpad to make that part easier.

And instead of starting with a blank canvas, I had:

→ 1,000+ templates to quickly find a layout that fits the app

→ 3D devices + hand device mockups to make screenshots feel more like actual product visuals

→ 10,000+ graphics and elements for customising them without jumping between design tools

→ Localization for adapting store creatives to different languages

→ A drag-and-drop editor that made changing layouts, text and elements ridiculously simple

The 3D + hand device mockups were probably my favourite part.

A normal screenshot shows the interface.

Putting it inside a polished device mockup makes it feel like a product.

And the templates saved me from staring at a blank canvas thinking:

“Okay... how do I make this look App Store worthy now?” 😭

One little tip if you’re creating your own App Store visuals:

Don’t use screenshots just to show screens.

Use each one to sell ONE reason to download.

Screenshot 1 → biggest outcome
Screenshot 2 → strongest feature
Screenshot 3 → how it works
Screenshot 4 → another use case/benefit

That way your gallery tells a story instead of becoming five pretty UI screenshots with no message.

If you’re preparing an iOS or Android app for launch, AppLaunchpad is worth trying:

https://lnkd.in/dC4766ph

Build the app.

Then make the store page actually sell it.
